title: Ubisoft Could Be The Company That Keeps Marvel’s Blade Alive
description: Time is running out for Arkane Lyon to find a buyer, but Ubisoft could acquire the Marvel's Blade developer, according to a new report. Arkane was one of several studios that Xbox divested itself of earlier this year, and while most of those developers have since gone on to become indie studios again-- except for Ninja Theory, which is expected to be closed after deals fell through--Arkane has found itself in a tough spot as it navigates life after Microsoft. Bloomberg reported that Ubisoft was in talks with Microsoft to acquire Arkane Lyon and help it finish work on Marvel's Blade. The report added that Microsoft is also exploring selling Arkane Lyon back to its management, but if plans fall through before a deal can be struck by December, it looks likely the studio will ultimately be shut down. Bloomberg claims Ubisoft is one of three companies that have submitted bids for Arkane Lyon, but it has not yet revealed the identities of the other two bidders. Arkane Lyon moving to Ubisoft does make sense on paper, as both the developer and the Assassin's Creed publisher are based in France. At the same time, Ubisoft has embarked on a major restructuring process throughout 2026, setting up new Creative Houses to spearhead development on its biggest franchises and downsizing operations across the globe. Recently, Ubisoft laid off 72 people from its Skull & Bones developer, Ubisoft Singapore, and Trials studio RedLynx might be shut down next. Marvel's Blade was announced at The Game Awards in December 2023, and since then, Arkane has gone radio silent about the game's status. Reports say it's close to completion and could launch in Q4 2027 if Arkane Lyon can keep working on it under a new publisher.

title: Steam Is Tightening Its Game Submission Rules As AI Slop Floods The Store
description: Valve currently has a review backlog on Steam, as the mandatory QA check every game must pass before launch on the platform has reportedly seen wait times balloon from a few days to over two weeks. The problem appears to be a massive number of builds, thought to be AI slop, that fail basic technical checks and are sent back for re-reviews, gumming up the works. To make headway and reduce back-and-forth friction, Valve has announced it's tightening the rules on what developers must verify before submitting builds. According to Valve, developers must ensure their games can run through Steam for at least five minutes, since the platform often receives builds that have never launched through Steam. Developers must also explicitly state whether their game requires common components like DirectX, Visual C++, or.NET so Steam knows to install them automatically, and, if advertised, prove that cloud saves work. On top of that, Steam will run automated checks to flag broken or incomplete achievements, and it will enforce stricter image categories. This is to ensure that players aren't misled by non-gameplay images posing as screenshots. Finally, dynamic reminders will pop up in the submission portal to nudge developers to deliver the content they originally promised. Is this a response to a flood of AI slop content on Steam lately? Valve didn't directly refer to that content, but as the recent Next Fest proved, mass-produced asset flips and AI-generated shovelware were everywhere. Content like that could be choking Steam's manual review queue, and indie game platform Itch.io addressed it this week with new guidelines for submitting games. Requiring developers to prove they've actually booted up their game and tested basic features through Steam could bring the review process back to manageable times, but it's not a silver bullet for the bad actors out there. Developers can voluntarily disclose that AI assisted in some form in building a game, and according to Game Discovery…

title: Fate of the Galaxy is a huge, fully-featured Star Wars space combat sim that, thanks to being a total conversion mod for Freespace Open, even runs on my rubbish laptop
description: Star Wars has been back in the news recently because, to cut a long story short, the US alt-right have decided that Darth Vader was actually the good guy. We are not here to indulge such buffoonery. We are here to talk about Fate of the Galaxy, a free unofficial space combat simulator set during the events of the original Star Wars trilogy, featuring several mission-based campaigns and a stable of Imperial and Rebel Alliance ships that ranges from the quad-blasting X-Wing to Boba Fett's Firespray 31. Also, Naboo starfighters, if you really must. It's a total conversion of poor dead Volition 's venerable dogfighter FreeSpace 2, running on the open source Free Space 2 Open engine via the popular Knossos launcher. You don't need a copy of FreeSpace 2 to play it. You also don't need to pay. And nor do you need a whizbang PC – this bucket of bolts hums along happily on my i5-1145G7 with no dedicated graphics card. As the Rancor said to the padawan: finally, some good food. Read more

title: How To Safely Pack Your PS5 For A Trip To New Zealand So You Can Play GTA 6 Early
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is almost here, and the first people to play it will be those lovely folks in New Zealand. Developer Rockstar Games has announced that GTA 6 will officially be ready to play at midnight local time on November 19, 2026, so it looks like the Kiwis are getting a significant head start. What's an eager GTA fan with a PlayStation 5 console in a later time zone supposed to do? Be patient? Hell no--not when you can grab a quick flight and start playing hours ahead of the rest of the world. Why can't I just change my PS5 region? Xbox Series X|S owners won't need to brave the horrors of coach on an international flight because they can easily change their region, but PS5 owners don't have that luxury. Sony hard-locks every PlayStation Network account to the region where it was originally created, so if you set up your account in a country other than New Zealand, you're out of luck, even if you have flown to New Zealand. That means you'll have to set up a new PSN account with New Zealand as your region and buy GTA 6 with New Zealand Dollar-denominated PlayStation Network gift cards from an online key retailer. This isn't exactly safe, but if you're seriously considering flying to New Zealand just to play the game a day early, I'm guessing you're willing to take a chance. When should I aim to fly? I'm going to assume you want to download GTA 6 at home, since hotel Wi-Fi networks in Auckland rarely provide the bandwidth to smoothly download a huge 200GB file without throttling or dropping connections. Ideally, fly from Los Angeles or San Francisco to Auckland, and book a flight that departs on November 10 at night after you're done preloading (if your internet is fast enough). That means you'll land on November 12, and the flight will take roughly 13 hours. You're also gaining 21 hours relative to LAX time, so you'll have a few days to shake off any jet lag. What am I supposed to do for the next week? Dude, you're in New Zealand, one of the coolest countries…

title: Link’s Ocarina Playing In The Remake Is So Accurate You Could Learn From It
description: Music has been a major part of The Legend of Zelda almost from the beginning, from the flute in A Link to the Past to the Wind Fish instruments of Link's Awakening. It played a titular role in Ocarina of Time, as a magical object tied to both the narrative and several gameplay elements. You would learn several different songs during your adventure, and for the Ocarina 2026 remake, Nintendo has taken it up a notch with finger movements so accurate you could use them to actually learn how to play the ocarina yourself. For an expert perspective, we turned to Eric Bernard, manager of Songbird Ocarina. For you longtime fans, this is the same company whose ads were ubiquitous in Nintendo Power magazine for years following the original release of Ocarina of Time. And Bernard said that based on the videos of Link in pre-release trailers, the playing was extremely accurate--with one minor caveat. "What we noticed from the animations of Link playing the Ocarina in the remake, is that he is always playing the song in the exact same key signature that each song was originally written in the original Ocarina of Time game," he said. "The fingering pattern when Link plays each song is also surprisingly very accurate, with just one general exception due to the physical limitations of the instrument." Bernard said the one exception is a product of the note range of the actual instrument being depicted. That range isn't quite large enough to capture all of the notes needed for some songs, so Nintendo had to get a little creative. "A standard 12-Hole Alto C ocarina such as the one depicted in the remake has a musical range of almost two octaves from A4 - F6," he said. "However, some songs that Link plays on the ocarina in the original key have notes that surpass the possible range of the actual ocarina. "For example, when we see Link play the Sun's Song, the highest note that the song ends on is a high G. However, an ocarina can not normally possibly reach a high G. The highest note…

title: The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Shows That A Masterpiece Is Ageless
description: 2026's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a reverent remake, remaining true to all the silliness and solemnity of the original, modernizing some gameplay elements with an elegance that feels so natural, it's as if it had always been there, and respecting the original design ethos enough to trust that all of the exploration and adventure will still feel great. For fans, to play this remake is to remember over and over again why you fell in love with Ocarina in the first place, and to see the brilliance with fresh eyes. For newcomers, this is now the definitive way to experience this all-time classic, and it's a can't-miss Switch 2 exclusive for everyone else. In case you're coming to this entirely fresh, Ocarina of Time was the first 3D Zelda game. This is the game that established series mainstays like Epona, Z-targeting, and the Goron and Gerudo. The Zelda series would not be the same without Ocarina of Time, so it holds a special place in the hearts of Zelda fans and in the history of Nintendo. Alongside Super Mario 64, this set the template for decades of the company's development. And since Nintendo tends to blaze trails that others follow, it was also remarkably influential on the industry as a whole. The most noticeable change to Ocarina 2026, naturally, is to the presentation, and the upgrade is stellar. Put simply, this is one of the best-looking Switch 2 games and a showpiece for the system. Link and the Kokiri children have been given careful plant-fiber stitching to their clothes, driving home the idea that they're forest sprites innately connected to the woods they occupy. Light glints off the titular Ocarina of Time as if it's a real piece of glazed ceramic. The brick textures of dungeons look decrepit and lived-in, and become spookier when lit by the dim glow of your fairy friend, Navi. Boss creatures crumble into purple ash and collapse into dust when defeated. Every piece of this world has been lovingly crafted, and as a returning fan, I was…

title: Guild Wars Is Getting Its First New Expansion In Almost 20 Years
description: ArenaNet may be hard at work on a new entry in the Guild Wars series, but it apparently won't stop it from releasing brand-new content for the 21-year-old original. Guild Wars Afterlife has just been announced, and it's a full paid expansion for Guild Wars arriving next January. Excitingly for old-school Guild Wars fans, Afterlife seems to bring back some content from the long-cancelled Utopia campaign, including the mystical, Mesoamerican-inspired setting of Xotecha. The new expansion will take players away from the continent of Tyria and into the Mists to explore the lost land of the dead. The expansion's mechanics seem to be purpose-built for replayability. Xotecha's new dungeon is an ever-changing expanse called the Unformed, where no two runs will be the same. This dynamic design even extends to your character build, with a custom skill-drafting mechanic allowing you to change up your abilities on the fly. While the skill-drafting mechanic seems unique to Xotecha, playing through Afterlife lets players unlock rewards they can take back with them out of the Mists. Afterlife will be the second true expansion for the original Guild Wars, after 2007's Eye of the North. Players looking to get into the new expansion will need Guild Wars Reforged, the 2025 re-release of the original game. Alongside Reforged, ArenaNet continues to support 2012's Guild Wars 2, while the brand-new Guild Wars 3 is also in the works. When the new game was announced, ArenaNet said it was committed to "actively developing all three games at the same time," and the Afterlife announcement shows the studio isn't taking that promise lightly. Guild Wars Afterlife will launch on PC, Steam, the App Store, and Google Play on January 13, 2027. The expansion will retail for $30 at full price, but ArenaNet is offering a discounted pre-order price of $24.

title: This Custom Xbox-Inside-An-Alligator Console Is Actually One Big Ad For GTA 6
description: Given that Sony holds the marketing rights for Grand Theft Auto 6, Microsoft has had to get creative to promote the open-world crime game for Xbox--and the company's latest effort in that department goes big. Say Hello to the X-Bite, a playable Xbox Series X console that was designed to look like it was swallowed whole by one of Florida's millions of alligators. Microsoft only made one of these ornate consoles, and you have to win a contest to get it. Microsoft's blog post doesn't mention GTA 6 or Rockstar Games, but Xbox marketing boss Josh Munsee said the system has "pure Miami vibes," and that's a pretty obvious reference to GTA 6 given the game takes place in a stand-in, Vice City, for the popular Florida city. The blog post says the winner of the console can play "some of the biggest games of the year" using it, and that's no doubt another nod to GTA 6. "This November, Xbox is heading to Florida--home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe," Microsoft said in its announcement of the X-Bite. The X-Bite is about five feet long, and the console itself sits inside the alligator, with the Nexus/Guide button illuminated through the gator's skin. The lucky winner will also get a custom Xbox controller with simulated bite marks on it. The custom console was designed by creature animatronic specialist John Nolan Studio, which did work for The Witcher and Jurassic World Dominion. Microsoft's fine print states that the gator console is a "custom fabrication" and wasn't made from a real alligator. "No actual alligators were used or harmed in the making of this console," Microsoft said. The estimated value of the console is $800, Microsoft said. The X-Bite. You can enter for a chance to win the X-Bite by following Xbox on X, Instagram, or TikTok, reposting the sweepstakes post, and then add #XbiteSweepstakes to your repost. You'll also need to have a public account. The sweepstakes runs now through November…

title: Don’t Make Me Pick A Favorite Dog In This Co-Op Game
description: Before I jumped into Gravhounds, the new third-person co-op shooter from Octopus Panic, the most pressing questions on my mind were centered on gameplay. In trailers, it seemed to have touches of both Helldivers 2 and Deep Rock Galactic, so I wondered which it resembled more. I saw elements of physics-based gameplay, so I was curious how chaotic that might get. With its alien worlds, I was eager to know what exploration was like. But once I finally got into the game, I was struck by a more immediate conundrum: Which dog do I pick? Out now in early access on PC and consoles, Gravhounds is a third-person shooter with tower-defense and extraction elements. It is a little like Helldivers 2, a bit more like Deep Rock Galactic, and the physics of its world are fun, but damn, I took a long time picking which doggo hero to play as. Currently, there are five characters to choose from, each with their own strengths, weaknesses, and special abilities. Though these are the aspects of a hero-based shooter that typically give me pause on a character-select screen, here they were merely secondary to the look and biography of each powerful pup. Dozer is an English Bulldog who is meant to play the tank role of the group. I practically never use the tank role, as I strongly prefer mobility to health whenever I can choose, but his blue-collar attire is easy to love, and the tag on his ear makes me root for him. What jerk did that? I get that it may mean he's up to date on his vaccines, and that's great, but can't we think of a different system? He's already fighting aliens from 9 to 5. Let's give his ears a break. Selene is an all-rounder with no major strengths or weaknesses in her attributes. That likely makes her a good starting class for most folks, which is pretty neat considering she seems to be a Weimaraner, often remembered as the dogs from Sesame Street. In a way, she was a lot of kids' first dog, too. Though those dogs from Jim Henson's world had human hands mimicking human…

title: WoW: Forever Shamans Are Protesting Class Changes After Being “Completely Ignored”
description: World of Warcraft: Forever just received a massive batch of class-balance updates ahead of launch that have boosted power across the board, but one group of players isn't happy with the changes: Shamans. Developer Blizzard recently released Forever's launch patch notes based on feedback and data accumulated during the beta, resulting in a power spike for all classes and major reworks for classes like Paladin and Rogue. Shamans, too, received some significant changes, most notably the removal of a key Elemental specialization ability, Lava Burst, along with any interactions other abilities had with it. It's that change, and other changes to specialization-specific abilities like Restoration's Riptide and Enhancement's Maelstrom Weapon, that have resulted in the WoW Classic Shaman Discord going into lockdown in protest. The entire server, which has around 80,000 members, has been made read-only, with a message declaring the reason for why it took what it described as such a "drastic measure." "Community feedback gets completely ignored and class fantasies are getting destroyed," the server declared. "With this we intend to give them [Blizzard] a sign and show them that the community is not [happy] with how they approached our beloved class. Give us back our class and spec identities and fantasies." While the protest is in regards to class changes in Forever specifically, the server is also home to Shaman discussions as they relate to other "classic" versions of the game as well, including WoW Classic and Mists of Pandaria Classic. As of writing, all of those channels are also locked and set to read-only. In a follow-up post, the server went into more detail about its complaints in regards to how Blizzard has approached Forever's Shaman design. It stated its complaints aren't about "damage output." It also made clear the server will re-open "regardless of the outcome," but that it felt like its feedback through "legitimate" channels were being ignored. The server then…

title: The Curse Of Star Wars Battlefront 3
description: I think Star Wars Battlefront 3 might be cursed. For the past 20 years, several different game studios have attempted to create a third entry in Star Wars’ premier shooter sub-series, yet have failed over and over again. We learned last week that EA is reportedly developing Battlefront 3, but also that the project came at the cost of shutting down BioWare. Battlefront 3 has always seemed like a no-brainer to make; 2005’s Star Wars: Battlefront 2 is widely beloved, and more personally, my favorite game of all time. Yet, the video game industry has never been able to actually launch a third installment in the popular series despite multiple attempts. After Pandemic Studios released Battlefront 2 in 2005, it would’ve made sense for the studio to roll right into making a third game, but that didn’t happen. In a 2025 interview with VideoGamer, game designer Dan Nanni revealed that Pandemic started work on a follow-up, but negotiations fell through as the console generation shifted and Pandemic couldn’t meet LucasArts' one-year deadline, reflecting the additional challenges of developing a big-budget licensed game. This wouldn’t be the last time a set-in-stone deadline would get a Battlefront game canceled. In lieu of making a new game with Pandemic Studios, LucasArts pursued a partnership with TimeSplitters developer Free Radical Design. This relationship led to what has become the best-known (and most infamous) prototype of Star Wars Battlefront 3. Leaked footage shows how this take on Battlefront 3 would’ve been a very ambitious, large-scale shooter, wherein players could fight on a planet’s surface, then get in a ship, take off, and fight in space. Plenty of footage from this take on Battlefront 3 has leaked over the years, so we have a somewhat good idea of what could’ve been. Some developers have even claimed the game was between 75% and 95% finished and that LucasArts was at one point interested in greenlighting a sequel, but Free Radical’s Battlefront 3 was never…

title: WoW: Forever Won’t Get More Class Balance Changes Any Time Soon
description: World of Warcraft: Forever is gearing up for launch with some major class balance changes, but don't expect any more for at least a month. As detailed in Forever's launch patch notes, Blizzard is making some dramatic class changes, including major reworks to Rogue and Paladin talents, in time for release that will result in a big spike in player power. Blizzard said it has used all the data from the game's month-long beta to "get everything tuned to a reasonable place." However, don't expect additional changes in the near future. Blizzard said it won't be making significant balance changes until sometime next month. "With the exception of bugs and serious outliers, we don't plan on making big tuning changes between now and the opening of the raids next month," Blizzard wrote in its patch notes. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data." Forever's three launch raids will open December 9, meaning there will be a little over a month without class changes. But launch and its subsequent months will just be the beginning, Blizzard said. "This is all merely a starting point for the classes in Forever, which will continue over the course of the months and years ahead just as they did following the original launch in 2004," Blizzard said. Blizzard is in it for the long haul with Forever, telling GameSpot in an interview it hopes the game will continue to receive updates for the next 10-20 years (or potentially forever). It recently announced its plans to release major Forever content updates every four months, as well as teased how its controller support will eventually lead to players being able to play the MMORPG on "whatever you want." WoW: Forever launches November 4, but you can make your character now. title: GTA 6 Is Getting A Physical Map–Here’s How To Get One For Free Or Very Cheap
description: Rockstar Games has confirmed more details about Grand Theft Auto 6 's impending release on November 19, including more information about physical goodies. While the game itself won't be available on a disc, Rockstar is offering a printable physical GTA 6 cover art poster and a map of the game's setting, Leonida. The poster and Leonida map will be available for free as digital downloads on GTA 6's official website on November 19. A double-sized physical version of the poster will be available "shortly after launch" from the Rockstar Store for 99 cents. Alternatively, it's free with any purchase from the Rockstar Store. Back in the day, Rockstar used to include fold-out posters in the box for GTA games featuring the game's cover art and map. But GTA 6 is a digital-only game. Players can buy a physical GTA 6 box at retail stores, but it won't include a disc, only a code for a digital download. Rockstar hasn't said if it will include anything extra in the box. Some retailers are apparently trying to sweeten the deal to encourage people to buy from them. It was recently reported that Walmart orders of GTA 6 will include some kind of "surprise." When the Switch 2 released, some Walmart orders for the console included "game-ready" snacks like soda and chips. In other news, Rockstar just recently announced when GTA 6 preloading begins and when the game unlocks--players in the US will be among the last people in the world to get in.
